title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Design Specs, Roadmap & Pricing (vNext)
author: Sofia Patel
body:
Overview
-------

This document consolidates the product overview, PRD (requirements & acceptance criteria), high-level design specs, roadmap & themes, pricing & packaging notes, and release guidance for the next major Unified Inference release (vNext). It is intended for product, engineering, SRE, sales, and solutions engineering stakeholders.

Goals of vNext
- Deliver a single developer-first inference surface across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes with consistent SLAs and predictable unit economics.
- Reduce per-token cost by 15–30% for typical L2–L3 conversational workloads through smarter routing, cache/batching improvements, and quantization profiles.
- Provide clear upgrade/migration paths and tooling for enterprise customers on Dedicated/Private.

1) Product Overview (Executive summary)
- Target users: ML Engineers and Software Engineers embedding LLMs into production applications (chat, generation, embeddings, reranking).
- Key capabilities delivered in vNext:
  - Unified API surface with model routing policies (latency/cost/region/tier) and programmatic override.
  - Integrated cost optimizer: per-route recommendations (batch sizing, quantization profile, cache TTLs).
  - Expanded model catalog: 3 new Redwood-verified open models and automatic compatibility mapping to quantized variants.
  - Improved Dedicated autoscaling policies (predictive scaling based on commit and burst capacity).
  - Private deployment tooling: automated network checks and on-prem packaging improvements for air-gapped installs.

2) PRD: Requirements & Acceptance Criteria
2.1 Objectives
- Primary Objective: Make it straightforward for customers to run high-quality LLM inference at predictable latency and cost across deployment modes.
- Secondary Objectives: Increase adoption of Dedicated by 20% and reduce customer-reported performance regressions by 50%.

2.2 Success metrics (quantitative)
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 450ms for 512-token request on hosted-prod region for Redwood-verified models.
- Cost: Average per-token cost improvement >= 20% for benchmarked customer workloads vs vPrev baseline.
- Reliability: API availability >= 99.95% (rolling 30d) for hosted tiers; Dedicated SLA improvements to 99.9% for reserved capacity.
- Adoption/Business: Dedicated activations +20% Q/Q; NPS for performance-related questions +10 pts.

2.3 Key user stories (must-haves)
- As an ML engineer, I can pin a route to a cost-optimized quantized model variant while preserving output quality within a configured regression threshold.
- As an SRE, I can configure routing policies that prefer low-latency hosts for premium customers and cost-optimized hosts for non-critical traffic.
- As an enterprise admin, I can run the private installer in air-gapped mode and validate network and KMS integration preflight checks.

2.4 Non-functional requirements
- Backwards compatibility: All existing API request shapes remain supported. Config API additions are additive-only.
- Security & compliance: Private deploys must support customer-managed KMS and produce audit logs for model inference requests for 90 days.
- Observability: Per-route token-level cost and latency breakdowns must be exposed in Console and via metrics (prometheus format).

2.5 Acceptance tests
- Automated perf harness runs against benchmark set: pass if cost improvement and latency targets met.
- Regression tests use gold prompt suites; quality drop <= 2 ROUGE points or equivalent metric for defined prompts.
- Private installer end-to-end validated in customer staging environment (network, KMS, storage).

3) Design specs (high-level)
3.1 Architecture changes
- Smart Router: new routing layer component (smart-router) that consumes policy config and runtime signals (latency, queue depth, cost per token estimate) and returns target model variant and host pool.
- Cost Optimizer: offline component that analyzes route-level telemetry and recommends batch sizes, cache TTLs, and quantization profiles. Recommendations surface in Console and API.
- Model Catalog Enhancements: metadata for quantized variants, compatibility matrix, and verified performance profile.

3.2 API changes (public)
- POST /v1/generate -> same shape; new optional query param: routing_policy=\"cost|latency|region:<region>|custom:<policy-id>\"
- PATCH /v1/routes/{route_id} -> new fields: preferred_quant_profile, cache_ttl_seconds, batch_hint
- GET /v1/recommendations/{route_id} -> returns optimizer suggestions (read-only)

3.3 Configuration table (example)
| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| preferred_quant_profile | string | \"fp16\" | One of [fp16, int8, int4]. Preference for runtime variant.
| cache_ttl_seconds | int | 60 | KV/prefix cache TTL for route-level caching.
| batch_hint | int | 8 | Suggested batch size for route.
| routing_policy | string | \"latency\" | Global routing policy fallback.

3.4 Runtime considerations
- Kernel selection: runtime must prefer quantization-friendly kernels for int8/int4 variants; fallback to fp16 when kernel not available.
- KV cache handshake: new header X-Cache-Policy returned in streaming responses with cache_hydrated=true/false for tracing.

3.5 Example CLI & JSON config
- CLI: redwoodctl routes update --route-id R123 --preferred-quant-profile int8 --cache-ttl 30 --batch-hint 12
- Example JSON: 
```
{
  \"route_id\": \"R123\",
  \"preferred_quant_profile\": \"int8\",
  \"cache_ttl_seconds\": 30,
  \"batch_hint\": 12
}
```

4) Roadmap & Themes (quarterly view)
- Q1 2027: Launch Smart Router MVP, cost optimizer beta, 2 quantized model variants in catalog, Public API & Console surfacing.
- Q2 2027: Dedicated autoscaling improvements, Private installer air-gap improvements, expand model catalog (+3 models).
- Q3 2027: SLA-backed Dedicated rollout, advanced rollout policies (canary by latency), GA cost optimizer.
- Q4 2027: Enterprise-focused integrations (marketplace listings, KMS/HSM deeper integrations), cross-region routing GA.

Roadmap themes:
- Performance & Cost: primary theme for FY27 H1.
- Enterprise-readiness: Compliance, private installs, SLAs.
- Developer Experience: simplified API and Console recommendations.

5) Pricing & Packaging notes
5.1 Pricing impact overview
- Hosted API: no change to base per-token rate at launch; introduce optional 'Cost-Optimized' route flag that applies a 10% discount when using quantized-compatible model variants (quality guardrails apply).
- Dedicated: new reserved capacity SKU tiers that include Optimizely credits (monthly recommendations and consulting). Expect +15% ASP for premium SLA tiers.
- Private: licensing modeled as platform fee + annual support; add-on for extended observability retention and compliance evidence.

5.2 Packaging recommendations
- Free & Starter: access to unified API; cost-optimizer recommendations visible but actionable for paid tiers only.
- Professional: includes cost-optimized routing for up to 3 routes, 30-day observability retention.
- Enterprise: full feature set (dedicated autoscale, private installer support, 90-day audit logs, premium SLA).

5.3 Sales & Enablement bullets
- Key messages: \"Same API, predictable cost—any model, any deployment.\" Emphasize measurable cost improvements and performance parity.
- Objection handling: If customers worry about quality loss with quantization, point to regression guardrails, AB testing, and rollback policies.

6) Release notes & rollout plan (vNext beta -> GA)
6.1 Beta (internal + pilot customers; target start 2026-12-28)
- Scope: Smart Router MVP, cost optimizer beta (read-only), 2 quantized variants in catalog, Console readouts.
- Pilot customers: 6 customers (mix of startups and tier-1 enterprise).
- Metrics to validate: cost delta vs baseline, p95 latency, quality regression checks on gold prompts.

6.2 GA (target 2027-03-15)
- Scope: Full Smart Router, writable cost recommendations, Dedicated autoscaling improvements, Private installer updates.
- Rollout steps:
  1. Feature flag rollout to 5% of hosted traffic (monitor latency, errors, cost).
  2. Gradual increase to 25% over 72 hours if no regressions.
  3. Open beta for Dedicated customers with toggle in Console.
  4. GA enablement and docs publish; migrate pilot customers with account teams.

6.3 Rollback & mitigation
- Automated rollback if p95 latency increases > 20% or quality regressions exceed thresholds for consecutive 4-hour windows.
- Fallback: Smart Router supports automatic fallback to pinned model variant (fp16) per route.

7) Ownership, stakeholders & success metrics
- Product owner: Sofia Patel (product)
- Engineering leads: Marcus Chen (serving-runtime), Anika Gupta (eng-platform), Liam O'Connor (eng-sre)
- SRE/Oncall: eng-sre oncall rotation + dedicated pager for pilot migrations
- Success metrics owner: Growth & Analytics team (weekly dashboards)

8) Documentation & runbooks (pre-launch checklist)
- Update API docs and SDKs with new routing_policy param (eng-developer-experience).
- Create runbook for Smart Router failures (eng-sre): detection rules, rollback playbook, emergency contact list.
- Publish Dedicated & Private migration guide with preflight checklists and sample Terraform snippets (eng-private-deployments).
